claims.text: The only GPS trace in this bundle is impaired for POLICY purposes, not merely for admissibility. EV-GPS-00110 carries a single 428.0 second gap between consecutive fixes, running 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, which is far over the 90 second limb of POL-RD-07(a), and its coverage of 81.7% is below the 90% mark. I disclose the impairment on the face of this claim: weight_multiplier 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE.

The dropout is not an incidental gap at the edge of the trip. It runs from the Defu Flyover portal fix to the Kallang portal fix, a 6.90 km straight line, and so covers the entire KPE tunnel stretch that the rider actually disputes. The one part of the route whose length decides this case is precisely the part this trace cannot measure, which is why the straight-line reconstruction is the driver-favourable reading POL-RD-07(i) mandates and not a finding about what was driven.

None of the independent corroborating sources POL-RD-07(ii) names is on file. The chat log contains no driver admission of any route other than the KPE - the driver's only message is 'going KPE ah boss' - and that log is itself truncated at 18:26:14, 2186 seconds before the trip ended (weight 0.60, issue TRUNCATED_LOG). The fare breakdown carries erp_gantries as null against a non-zero tolls_erp of 3.00 (weight 0.75, issue PARTIAL_RECORD), so the gantry-corridor test cannot be run at all, and I do not put it higher than that: the prepass is right that the missing itemisation is an incomplete record rather than proof of a phantom charge.

The trip record's actual_distance_km of 21.20 is not independent corroboration within POL-RD-07(ii). The admissibility note on EV-TRIP-00110 records that the figure is itself derived from the impaired trace and adds no independent evidence of distance, and the fare ledger's distance_charged_km is 21.20 as well. Two copies of one impaired measurement are not a second measurement, and the billed distance is expressly excluded as corroboration where it is a copy of the trace figure.

With the trace impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration anywhere in the bundle, POL-RD-07(iii) directs ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION: absence of proof on a broken trace is a data failure, not a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes escalation mandatory on the same facts. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held rather than collected, so escalation is the outcome that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge.

Independently of any corroboration question, the fact that decides this case is carried by an artifact at weight 0.39. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence may not exceed the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact, and the discount is not rescued by the trip record, because that artifact is derived from the same trace and is therefore not independent. A cap of 0.39 is below the 0.70 platform floor, so POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation on that ground alone.

The threshold question itself is undecided on this record and the case cannot be closed out. Measured the driver-favourable way that POL-RD-07(i) requires - the straight line across the gap - the trip is 21.20 km against an optimal of 18.40 km, an excess of 2.80 km and 15.2%, just under POL-RD-01's 20% establishment gate. The admissibility assessment on the same artifact records that a surface route between the same two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km and over that gate. Nothing in the bundle distinguishes the two readings, so a NO_ACTION that treats 21.2 km as settled fact would be resting on the very reconstruction the gap makes unreliable.

The driver has pointed to no clause and no artifact to exculpate the route. His assertion that he 'took the KPE like always' is a general assertion about the road he used, and POL-RD-08 requires a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00110-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 - no LTA advisory covers the KPE or the ECP in the 18:19-19:02 window - so POL-RD-03 closure exoneration has nothing behind it and cannot run.

No clause in this policy licenses 'my phone loses signal in the tunnel' as a reason to stand over the distance and time charged. The lost signal may explain the gap in the trace; it does not explain 2.80 km of driving beyond the platform's own optimal route, and it is not an exoneration under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12. It is relevant here only because it confirms the trace, not the route, is the thing that failed.

The rider is not a repeat claimant and the heightened corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08 does not bite. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the threshold of 4 that clause sets, and it is the only rider-profile field POL-RD-08 permits anyone to rely on for this test. There is no basis on this record for treating the claim as one that needs more than the ordinary evidence.

claims.text: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and says in terms that trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The trace records 21.20 km against a booked optimal of 18.40 km: an excess of 2.80 km, or 15.2% of optimal. The percentage limb of the establishment test requires the excess to exceed 20% of optimal; 20% of 18.40 km is 3.68 km and the excess is 2.80 km, so the limb fails. Both tests must pass, and POL-RD-01 provides that if either fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The trace is impaired at weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE; the point survives that discount because POL-RD-07(i) directs the excess across the impaired stretch to be measured as the straight line between the bounding fixes, which is the reading most favourable to the driver and is the reading I rely on.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: there is a single 428.0 s gap between consecutive fixes, more than four times the 90 s limb (a), running from the Defu Flyover portal fix to the Kallang portal fix. Under POL-RD-07(i) the excess across that stretch is the straight line between the bounding fixes, expressly because that is the reading most favourable to the driver. Measured that way the trip is 21.20 km and sits below the POL-RD-01 threshold. The 25.50 km surface-route figure that would cross the threshold is a reconstruction, not a measurement, and no artifact in this bundle carries it. The trace is impaired at weight 0.39 (GPS_GAP, LOW_COVERAGE).

A deviation may not be established on the gps_trace alone and must be corroborated by one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names. None is present. There is no driver admission in the chat log: the driver's only message says he is going by the KPE, which is the corridor the platform's own optimal route uses - optimal_route_source reads 'optimal is KPE then ECP, crossing both gantries'. erp_gantries is null, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The counterparty statement asserts the same KPE route and admits nothing. And trip_record.actual_distance_km is, on the pre-pass's own assessment, derived from this very trace, so it is not independent corroboration. The chat log is itself impaired at weight 0.6 with issue TRUNCATED_LOG (last message 18:26:14, 2,186 s before the trip ended); I do not assert what was said after that point. Without an independent source the claimed refund cannot be ordered.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). The trace is impaired - a 428.0 s gap and coverage of 81.7% - and no source in POL-RD-07(ii)'s list exists on this record. The second limb of the rider's burden is therefore not discharged and the driver is never put to an exculpatory clause at all.

The surviving chat shows the driver volunteering the corridor he was taking - 'going KPE ah boss' at 18:25:50 - and the rider answering 'ok' 24 seconds later, and the platform's own optimal route for this trip is the KPE then the ECP. The rider had notice of, and did not object to, the very corridor the platform routed him along, so the route driven is not an off-corridor route he can complain of. I do not put this forward as a POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour: no rider message identifies a place or road, and both waypoint_hint fields are null, so that clause is unavailable on this record and I do not rely on it. The chat log is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue TRUNCATED_LOG.

On the fare, no line is unmatched. The rider's own claim concedes $3.00 of ERP; the fare breakdown charges tolls_erp of 3.00, which equals trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd of 3.00 for a route the platform describes as crossing both gantries on the optimal corridor. Gantry-by-gantry matching is not possible because erp_gantries is null, and POL-RD-09(4) directs that where no coordinates are carried the match is undecidable, the line is treated as matched, and the ruling must say so. There is accordingly no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown is impaired at weight 0.75 with issue PARTIAL_RECORD.

The rider's complaint is really about the 39 minute duration. POL-RD-01's establishment test is a distance test - excess over the optimal distance measured on the trace. Elapsed time enters this policy only as optimal_duration_min inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and POL-RD-02 runs only where a deviation has already been established. No deviation is established here, so the metered time charge stands and the duration gives the rider no separate ground of complaint.

POL-RD-06's profile check is engaged only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, which requires excess above 50% of optimal or above 8.0 km. The excess here is 2.80 km and 15.2%, so the materiality gate is not reached, no pattern test is required and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is licensed. For completeness on the test the clause does name, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed_trips_90d over the same window: there is no repeat-deviation pattern and no conduct referral is open. Nor is this a case where POL-RD-06(a) could matter, because the case is not genuinely balanced - the excess fails the threshold on the reading most favourable to the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case is going to a human reviewer, and no money moves while that happens. Here is why, and what is undecided.

The single GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00110) contains one 428.0-second gap between consecutive fixes, from 18:35:00 to 18:42:08, running from the Defu Flyover portal fix to the Kallang portal fix (6.90 km apart in a straight line). That is more than four times the 90-second limb in POL-RD-07(a), and it covers the entire KPE tunnel stretch you are disputing. The trace is therefore impaired for policy purposes, not merely for the schema pre-pass, with weight_multiplier 0.39 and issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE; coverage is 81.7% against a 90% threshold (POL-GEN-02(3)).

Measured the way POL-RD-07(i) requires — the straight line between the bounding fixes, the reading most favourable to the driver — the trip is 21.20 km against a booked optimal of 18.40 km: an excess of 2.80 km, or 15.2%, just under POL-RD-01's 20% establishment limb. A surface route between the same two portals would put the trip at 25.50 km, over that limb. Nothing in this bundle distinguishes the two readings, so the trace cannot settle whether a deviation exists, and the policy does not let me close the case as if it had.

POL-RD-07(ii) requires an impaired-trace deviation to be carried by an independent source, and I have checked each source that clause names; none is present. The chat log has no driver admission — the driver's only message is 'going KPE ah boss' at 18:25:50, which is the platform's own optimal corridor ('KPE then ECP'), and the log is itself truncated at 18:26:14, 2,186 s before the trip ended (EV-CHAT-00110, weight 0.60, TRUNCATED_LOG). erp_gantries is null in the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00110, weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD), so no charged gantry places the vehicle off the optimal corridor; under POL-RD-09(4) a line with no coordinates is treated as matched, and I record that the $3.00 ERP therefore shows no billing-integrity defect. The counterparty statement says only that the driver took the KPE, which is the optimal corridor, and admits nothing. And trip_record.actual_distance_km (21.20) is, on the pre-pass's own note, derived from this same trace, so it is a copy of one measurement, not a second one.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists, POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) require escalation rather than a finding for the driver. Independently, the fact that decides this case — how far was actually driven — is carried only by an artifact at weight 0.39, and the trip record and fare ledger are copies of that same measurement rather than independent carriers, so POL-GEN-02(2) caps my confidence at 0.39, below the 0.70 floor, and POL-RD-10(1) fires on that ground as well.

I have answered the parties' surviving arguments on the merits. For the driver: POL-RD-01's percentage limb does fail on the current reading; elapsed time is not a separate ground, because POL-RD-02 only runs once a deviation is established; POL-RD-06 is not engaged (no material deviation, and deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 744 completed trips in 90 days, so no conduct referral is open); the chat is not a POL-RD-04 rider-requested detour; and the fare shows no billing-integrity failure. For the rider: POL-RD-08's heightened corroboration requirement does not bite, because deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the threshold of 4. None of this changes the outcome, because the trace cannot measure the stretch that decides the case.

What would resolve it: any one independent source POL-RD-07(ii) names — a complete, untruncated chat log containing a driver admission; itemised erp_gantry coordinates for this trip; a counterparty statement admitting the route; or a trip distance derived independently of this trace. The disputed $34.42 is held, not collected or refunded, until the reviewer sees one of those. No referral is issued, because no clause produces one here: POL-RD-06(c) needs a material deviation or an established pattern, and POL-RD-09(4) finds no unmatched charge line.

On the fare, no line is unmatched.
